hypotheses.claim: For D/E training, the dominant remaining specification risk is no longer the mathematical form of U/D/U(d)/f but authority leakage: if evidence independence, event identity or test admissibility can be asserted by the row producer, the labeler can be deterministic yet still teach circular epistemics.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: A fully closed synthetic task-world may legitimately define all dependence/admissibility facts internally, making external evidence-producer authentication unnecessary for synthetic curriculum rows.
hypotheses.discriminator: Build one source-bound closed-world fixture where dependence, event digest, admissibility, execution and outcome are all mechanically derived; mutation-test every caller-provided shortcut. Positive D/E generation remains blocked until the retained v3/A02 proof chain accepts this exact construction under current authority.

hypotheses.claim: Dynamic episodic binding should be evaluated as an equivariance/generalization capability across codebook permutations and visible nuisance schedules, not by aggregate within-template accuracy.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Large balanced factorial corpora may still permit higher-order visible shortcuts that preserve aggregate and marginal metrics.
hypotheses.discriminator: Require model-visible semantic ablation/nuisance-only challenger, conditional MI/full-cross checks, unseen permutation/template/symbol factors and family/provenance separation on exact rendered bytes.

hypotheses.claim: Training channels for binder routing, symbolic reasoning, Hyperposition/GRF policy, DB-vs-simulation, variable-N coordination and Claude handoff should retain separate capability curves because one mixed full-FT score can hide channel regression.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: A single mixture could induce beneficial shared representations and outperform staged curricula without harmful interference.
hypotheses.discriminator: Matched-token curriculum schedule ablation with frozen per-channel OOD/retention gates and no aggregate-score masking.

external_research.finding: Transformers trained on symbolic variable dereferencing pass through shortcut phases before learning a systematic routing mechanism; causal interventions identify specialized routing heads/residual-stream memory in that trained setting.
external_research.project_implication: Keep shortcut, checkpoint and causal routing tests; do not infer the mechanism exists in the measured Qwen3.5 checkpoint.

external_research.finding: Symbol tuning with arbitrary labels improves use of in-context input-label mappings and flipped labels.
external_research.project_implication: Supports counterfactual episode-local codebook training pressure while remaining non-Qwen-specific evidence.

external_research.finding: Steering vectors can have positive mean effects while exhibiting high per-sample variance and opposite-sign effects; representation geometry predicts reliability.
external_research.project_implication: Do not replace training/evaluation with mean steering gains; require held-out reliability and off-target controls.

external_research.finding: Behaviorally equivalent steering interventions can be non-identifiable without structural assumptions; multi-environment/cross-layer constraints can improve identifiability.
external_research.project_implication: Preserve alternative J-Space hypotheses and require structural/multi-environment discrimination before treating a vector as uniquely semantic.
